title: Analysis of Local Protein Accumulation Kinetics by Live-Cell Imaging in Yeast Systems
author: Okada, MacTaggart, et al.

steps.title: Prepare YPD agar medium
steps.instruction: Make two mixtures for 1 L YPD agar: Mixture 1 – dissolve 10 g yeast extract, 20 g Bacto peptone and 20 g agar in distilled water up to 900 mL and add a magnetic stir bar; Mixture 2 – dissolve 20 g glucose in distilled water up to 100 mL. Autoclave both mixtures at 121 °C for 20 min, then combine Mixture 2 into Mixture 1 while stirring. Cool the medium at 22‑24 °C until it reaches 50‑55 °C, pour into ~30 Petri dishes, and let plates dry for 1‑2 days at 22‑24 °C. Store plates at 4 °C (in a plastic bag) for up to 6 months.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Mixture 1 (yeast extract, peptone, agar, water).
Prepare Mixture 2 (glucose, water).
Autoclave both mixtures (121 °C, 20 min).
Stir Mixture 2 into Mixture 1.
Cool to 50‑55 °C, pour ~30 plates.
Dry plates 1‑2 days at 22‑24 °C.
Store at 4 °C in a sealed bag (≤6 months).

steps.title: Prepare SC liquid medium
steps.instruction: Make two mixtures for 1 L SC minimal medium: Mixture 1 – grind 6.7 g yeast nitrogen base (without amino acids, with ammonium sulfate) together with 2 g of the amino‑acid mix (Table 1) and add distilled water up to 900 mL; Mixture 2 – dissolve 20 g glucose in distilled water up to 100 mL. Autoclave both at 121 °C for 20 min, cool to 22‑24 °C and store in the dark for ≤3 months. Just before use, mix Mixture 1 and Mixture 2 at a 9:1 ratio (v/v). Optional: adjust pH to 7 with NaOH if GFP signal is quenched (SC pH≈4.5). Optional: use premixed powder #1300‑030 (Sunrise Science) instead of grinding. Do not mix the two solutions immediately after autoclaving to avoid contamination.

substeps.instruction: Grind yeast nitrogen base (6.7 g) with amino‑acid mix (2 g).
Add water to 900 mL (Mixture 1).
Dissolve glucose (20 g) in water to 100 mL (Mixture 2).
Autoclave both mixtures (121 °C, 20 min).
Cool and store at 22‑24 °C, dark (≤3 months).
Just before use, combine Mixture 1:Mixture 2 = 9:1.
Optional pH adjustment to 7 with NaOH if needed.

steps.title: Prepare YE5S agar or liquid medium
steps.instruction: For 1 L YE5S medium, combine 5 g yeast extract, 30 g glucose, 0.2 g each of adenine, uracil, histidine, leucine and lysine, and for agar add 20 g agar; bring to 1 L with distilled water. Autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min. If preparing agar, cool to 50‑55 °C, pour ~30 plates, dry 1‑2 days at 22‑24 °C and store at 4 °C. If preparing liquid, simply cool to 22‑24 °C and store at the same temperature. Medium remains usable for ≥3 months.

substeps.instruction: Weigh reagents (yeast extract, glucose, adenine, uracil, histidine, leucine, lysine; agar if agar medium).
Add distilled water to 1 L.
Autoclave (121 °C, 20 min).
For agar: cool to 50‑55 °C, pour plates, dry 1‑2 days, store at 4 °C.
For liquid: cool to 22‑24 °C, store at 22‑24 °C.

steps.title: Streak yeast from glycerol stock
steps.instruction: Retrieve frozen glycerol stock (‑80 °C) and streak the strain of interest onto YPD plates (or YE5S plates for S. pombe). Incubate 1‑2 days at 25 °C or 30 °C. Seal plates with parafilm; plates can be kept at 4 °C for 3‑4 weeks. Do not use minimal medium plates for storage.

substeps.instruction: Streak strain onto appropriate rich plate.
Incubate 1‑2 days at 25 °C or 30 °C.
Seal with parafilm and store at 4 °C (≤4 weeks).

steps.title: Inoculate preculture in liquid medium
steps.instruction: A day before imaging, pick a single colony from the streaked plate and inoculate into 4 mL SC liquid medium in a 16 × 150 mm round‑bottom test tube (for S. cerevisiae) or 8 mL YE5S liquid medium in a 25 × 120 mm flat‑bottom tube (for S. pombe). Shake at 25 °C, 210 rpm for 6‑8 h. Avoid using YPD liquid medium for imaging because of high autofluorescence. Optional: make a thin cell patch on a fresh plate and incubate at 25 °C as an alternative.

substeps.instruction: Pick single colony.
Inoculate into 4 mL SC (or 8 mL YE5S for fission yeast).
Shake 25 °C, 210 rpm, 6‑8 h.

steps.title: Grow overnight culture to mid‑log
steps.instruction: Transfer the preculture into fresh 4 mL SC medium (or 8 mL YE5S for fission yeast) in a 16 × 150 mm (or 25 × 120 mm) test tube. Shake at 25 °C, 210 rpm overnight (12‑16 h) until the culture reaches OD₆₀₀ = 0.3‑0.7 (≈0.4‑1 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹). Calculate the inoculation volume with the provided spreadsheet (Table S1).

substeps.instruction: Transfer preculture to fresh medium (4 mL SC or 8 mL YE5S).
Shake 25 °C, 210 rpm, 12‑16 h.
Monitor OD₆₀₀; stop when 0.3‑0.7 (0.4‑1 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹).
Use spreadsheet to determine inoculation volume.

steps.title: Optional: Prepare multiple cultures
steps.instruction: To increase the chance of capturing cells at the desired growth phase, set up several parallel cultures by serially diluting the overnight culture, creating a broader range of cell densities for imaging.

steps.title: Process image sequences in Fiji
steps.instruction: Open the ND image sequence in Fiji (File > Open). Create a Z‑stack sum projection (Image > Stacks > Z Project, choose ‘Sum Slices’). Align the stack using the StackReg plugin (Plugins > Registration > StackReg, select ‘Rigid Body’). Note that processing a 512 × 512 pixel, 55‑slice stack takes ~15 s on a Xeon W‑2223 workstation or ~30 s on a Core i5‑2410M laptop.

substeps.instruction: Open ND file.
Create sum‑projection Z‑stack.
Run StackReg (Rigid Body).

steps.title: Define protein and background ROIs
steps.instruction: In the aligned stack, draw a polygon around the protein of interest (ROI ‘a’) using the Polygon tool and add it to the ROI Manager (Edit > Selection > Add to Manager or press T). Scroll through slices to ensure the polygon stays over the target throughout the series. Repeat to draw a background polygon (ROI ‘b’) and add it to the manager. Avoid using a cell‑free area as background if possible; intracellular background may fluctuate but is preferred over empty space.

substeps.instruction: Draw polygon for protein ROI (a) and add to manager.
Verify ROI a stays over target in all slices.
Draw polygon for background ROI (b) and add to manager.
Verify ROI b stays in background throughout.

steps.title: Measure integrated density and export data
steps.instruction: Open Analyze > Set Measurements and ensure ‘Integrated density’ is checked. In the ROI Manager, select both ROIs (click ROI a, hold Shift, click ROI b) and choose Multi‑Measure (More > Multi Measure). Check ‘Measure all slices’ and ‘One row per slice’. Save the results, open them in Excel, GraphPad, or R. Subtract the background integrated density (IntDen₂ from ROI b) from the protein integrated density (IntDen₁ from ROI a) to obtain corrected fluorescence values.

substeps.instruction: Set measurements to include Integrated density.
Select both ROIs in ROI Manager.
Run Multi‑Measure with both ‘Measure all slices’ and ‘One row per slice’ checked.
Save results and open in analysis software.
Subtract background IntDen₂ from IntDen₁.

steps.title: Analyze and summarize fluorescence kinetics
steps.instruction: Import the corrected intensity data into Excel (or another statistical program). Mark the image number that corresponds to a reference cell‑cycle event (e.g., spindle breakage) as time 0. Align all individual ROI datasets by this reference point, then plot fluorescence intensity versus time for each cell. Generate a summary plot showing mean ± standard deviation across cells, and also display individual traces to assess data quality.

substeps.instruction: Identify reference event slice (time 0).
Align each dataset to time 0.
Plot individual intensity traces.
Create summary plot (mean ± SD).
Inspect individual and summary plots for reliability.
